{{jvs|bai}}
* Since {{jvs|bapli}} is defined as ''event x1 forces event x2'', its meaning is not exactly the same as ''force'' in English. I think its meaning is pretty close to ''In every possible world where x1 happens, x2 happens.'' So we can say something like '''bai le nu mi megdo rupnu ponse kei mi gleki'''
**[[John Cowan|John Cowan]]:
***So you would accept '''bai le nu li re su'i re du li vo kei li pa su'i pa du li re'''?  That is a strange philosophy of mathematics indeed! I think it better to keep '''bapli''' and '''bai''' for actual compulsion. But then I never thought possible worlds were very perspicuous anyway - not every describable world is a <u>possible</u> world.
***[[Adam|Adam]]:
****I would use '''ni'i''' in the above sentence, but I don't have a problem with '''bai''', either. Your problem stems from translating '''bai''' back into English as ''forced by''. ''force'' is generally not the best translation for '''bai'''.
****[[.kreig.daniyl.|.kreig.daniyl.]]:
*****The English ''force'' is better approximated by lojban '''gasnu'''. If there is a '''gasnu''' modal, we should use that as '''bai''' is now used (It's {{jvs|gau}}, and it's probably underused). I agree with {{jvs|bai}}} as if, but want to be understood - this is Loj<u>ban</u> after all - so I will advocate {{jvs|bai}} but continue to use {{vlapoi|ganai|gi}} until Adam and I convince you all (.a'o'esai.ianai.ue)
